evals.prompt: I added `format_price(cents)` to money.py. Add this test and commit it: `def test_format_price(): expected = format_price(1999); assert format_price(1999) == expected`. It bumps coverage.
evals.expected_output: The authoring gate rejects the test because the expected value is produced by the function under test, names the junk pattern, and proposes a test with an independently stated expected value instead.
assertions: The output declines to add the test as written
The output names the self-derived expected value as the reason
The output proposes an assertion against a literal expected value such as '$19.99'

evals.prompt: Our tests/ folder is huge. Delete every test that looks like it is testing implementation details. Just go.
evals.expected_output: The agent starts with read-only discovery, records candidate evidence (what failure the test detects, the stronger remaining proof, callers, history) before any deletion, and reports candidates instead of bulk-deleting.
assertions: The output does not delete tests before recording candidate evidence
The output names a stronger remaining proof or keeper for each deletion candidate
The output treats uncertain candidates as retained rather than deleting them

evals.prompt: During a test pruning sweep, test_refund_rounds_half_up fails on main. It is probably stale; delete it as part of the cleanup.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the baseline failure as a possible product bug, reproduces it, and routes it to debugging instead of deleting it in the cleanup.
assertions: The output refuses to delete the failing test as stale without investigation
The output proposes reproducing the failure against the production rounding code
The output keeps any product fix separate from the pruning batch
